senses.gloss: (Parel of קָטַע) [to cut; cmp. גּוּז,] to caper, leap.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 38">Gen. R. s. 38</cite> <he>ארכיליסטיס מְקַרְטֵעַ</he> Ar. the chief robber (Satan) cuts his capers (ed. <he>השטן מקטרג</he>).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 74">Gen. R. s. 74</cite> <he>מְקַרְטְעִים בו</he> Var., v. <cite ref="S02182"><he>קִרְקֵר</he> II</cite>. Tanḥ. Ki Thissa 19 <he>נוער כשהוא מְקַרְטֵעַ</he> (read: <cite ref="T00011"><he>נראה</he></cite>) appearing as if it (the golden calf) were leaping, v. <cite ref="T00557"><he>רָטַט</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Chullin 75a:5">Ḥull. 75ᵃ</cite> <he>דג מקרטע</he> (Ms. H. <cite ref="S02015"><he>המִתְקַרְטֵעַ</he></cite>; Ms. R. 1 <he>המקורטע</he>; <cite ref="Chullin 2a">2</cite> <he>המטרטע</he> corr. acc.; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 2) a fish jumping (in the death agony); a. e.—

<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 40">Pesik. R. s. 40</cite> [read:] <he>שלא נראה המאכלת בא</he>(<cite ref="E00000"><he>ה</he></cite>) <he>עלי ונְקַרְטֵעַ ונִיפָּסֵל וכ׳</he> lest we (I) see the knife coming on me, and make a convulsive movement, and become unfit for a sacrifice; [Friedm. corrects: <he>שלא אראה … וַאֲקַרְטֵעַ ואִיפָּסֵל</he> lest I see the knife &c.]
